name: Selecting a slice of state
description: Passing a selector function to the store hook subscribes a component to only that piece of state, so it re-renders only when that specific value changes.
returns: The value returned by the selector.
example:
const bears = useBearStore((state) => state.bears);
// Component only re-renders when `bears` changes, not on unrelated state updates
notes: Avoid selecting the whole state object (useStore()) unless the component genuinely needs everything — it re-renders on every store change.

name: Selector functions as a core concept
description: In Zustand, the selector passed to the hook is the primary API for controlling re-renders — instead of memoizing components, you narrow what each component subscribes to.
example:
// Selects and derives in one step
const bearCount = useBearStore((state) => state.bears.length);
notes: Selectors can also compute derived values inline, avoiding extra state fields just for derived data.

name: Selecting multiple values
syntax: const { a, b } = useStore((state) => ({ a: state.a, b: state.b }))
description: A selector can return an object or array combining multiple state values, but by default a new object is created on every call, causing re-renders even when the underlying values haven't changed.
returns: An object or array of the selected values.
notes: Without a custom equality check, this pattern re-renders on every store update — pair it with useShallow to fix that.

name: useShallow()
syntax:
import { useShallow } from 'zustand/react/shallow'
const { a, b } = useStore(useShallow((state) => ({ a: state.a, b: state.b })))
description: useShallow wraps a selector so the returned object/array is compared with shallow equality, preventing re-renders when the selected values themselves haven't changed.
parameters: selector — function returning an object or array of selected values.
returns: The selected object/array, memoized by shallow comparison across renders.
notes: This is the recommended replacement for the older shallow equality function passed as a second hook argument in Zustand v4.

name: shallow equality function
description: shallow is a standalone comparator that checks top-level equality between two objects/arrays, used internally by useShallow and available for manual comparisons.
returns: true if all top-level keys/values are reference-equal, false otherwise.
example:
import { shallow } from 'zustand/shallow';
shallow({ a: 1 }, { a: 1 }); // true
notes: In Zustand v4 this could be passed directly as a second argument to the store hook; v5 recommends useShallow instead.

name: Selecting whole state (anti-pattern)
description: Calling the store hook with no selector returns the entire state object and subscribes the component to every change in the store.
example:
// Re-renders on ANY store change, even unrelated fields
const state = useBearStore();
notes: Reserve this for debugging or components that truly depend on most of the store — otherwise select only what you need.
